title: app-riset-pdp: Client-Side Face Detection Benchmarking Instrument (OpenCV.js vs face-api.js)
abstract: A self-contained, client-side face detection benchmarking instrument (single HTML/JavaScript page, no build step) comparing two in-browser face detection pipelines — OpenCV.js (Haar Cascade, LBP histogram, cosine similarity, threshold >= 0.85) and face-api.js (TinyFaceDetector, 68-point landmarks, 128-D descriptor, euclidean distance, threshold <= 0.60) — under a controlled 36-scenario factorial design (3 lighting levels x 4 pose angles x 3 device tiers). Provides dual-engine identity enrollment, manual and automated trial capture, live per-engine latency/FPS-equivalent/memory metrics, aggregate and per-scenario precision/recall/F1-score summaries, CSV/JSON export, and a client-vs-server latency comparison module (real API call to the companion project api-riset-pdp on Cloudflare Workers, or network-parameter simulation). All biometric processing runs entirely in the browser (privacy-by-design). Developed to collect data for Sismadi, Manan, & Hartini (2026), 'Inovasi Media ICT Deteksi Wajah untuk Presensi Digital Mahasiswa: Analisis Akurasi dan Performa', ACADEMIA: Jurnal Inovasi Riset Akademik, 6(4), 3400-3408, under the Penelitian Dosen Pemula (PDP) grant at Universitas IPWIJA, Jakarta (n=180 observations per library, 50 student participants, closed-set verification).
